data.text:
## tabs — Tabs (component, archetype navigate)
A set of peer views sharing one space, one visible at a time, switched by labelled controls.
Aliases: tab bar, segmented control, tab strip
Anatomy: Tab (One label); Panel (The view it shows); Indicator (Which is current)
Related — uses: badge, menu | neighbors: view-switcher, accordion, carousel
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Placement and overflow [layout] — Where are tabs, and what happens when there are too many?
  - placement (single-select: one id) — Placement
      top: Top (e.g. Browser tabs)
      bottom: Bottom (e.g. iOS tab bars)
      vertical: Vertical (e.g. Edge vertical tabs)
      segmented-control: Segmented control (e.g. iOS segmented controls)
  - overflow (single-select: one id) — Overflow
      scroll: Scroll (e.g. Material scrollable tabs)
      shrink: Shrink (e.g. Chrome tabs)
      more-menu: More menu (e.g. Office ribbons)
      wrap: Wrap (e.g. Old desktop dialogs)
* Labels [content] — What does a tab say?
  - label (multi-select: list of ids) — Label content
      text: Text (e.g. GitHub repository tabs)
      icon: Icon (e.g. Bottom tab bars)
      badge-count: Badge count (e.g. Unread counts)
      favicon-and-title: Favicon and title (e.g. Browser tabs)
      close-button: Close button (e.g. Editor tabs)
* Tab origin and grouping [composition] — Who makes tabs, and can they be grouped?
  - origin (single-select: one id) — Origin
      fixed-by-the-designer: Fixed by the designer (e.g. Settings tabs)
      created-by-the-person: Created by the person (e.g. Browser tabs; CHI '25 probe overviews)
      saved-views: Saved views (e.g. Notion database views)
      pinned-and-preview-tabs: Pinned and preview tabs — A preview tab is replaced unless kept (e.g. VS Code preview tabs)
  - grouping (single-select: one id) — Grouping
      flat: Flat (e.g. Most tab sets)
      tab-groups: Tab groups (e.g. Chrome tab groups)
      nested-tabs: Nested tabs (e.g. Tabs inside a tab panel)
* Background tabs [lifecycle] — What happens to a tab you are not looking at?
  - background (single-select: one id) — Background state
      unloaded-on-switch: Unloaded on switch (e.g. Simple tab widgets)
      kept-alive: Kept alive (e.g. Editor tabs)
      put-to-sleep: Put to sleep (e.g. Edge sleeping tabs)
* Switching [invocation] — How does a person switch?
  - switchBy (multi-select: list of ids) — Switch by
      click: Click (e.g. All)
      swipe-between-panels: Swipe between panels (e.g. Android tab layouts)
      keyboard: Keyboard (e.g. Ctrl+Tab)
      search-tabs: Search tabs (e.g. Chrome tab search)

## carousel — Carousel (component, archetype browse-collections)
A horizontally scrolling strip that shows a subset of items at once and hides the rest off-screen.
Aliases: slider, shelf, horizontal scroller
Anatomy: Track (The items in order); Viewport (What is currently visible); Controls (Arrows, dots, swipe)
Related — uses: card, pagination | neighbors: stories, tabs
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Visible items [layout] — How many items are visible, and how?
  - visible (single-select: one id) — Visible items
      one-at-a-time: One at a time — A hero slide (e.g. Homepage hero carousels)
      peek-next: Peek next — The next item shows at the edge (e.g. App Store)
      multi-item-strip: Multi-item strip (e.g. Netflix rows)
      hero-with-smaller-neighbours: Hero with smaller neighbours (e.g. Material 3 hero carousel)
* Advancing [invocation] — How does it move?
  - advance (multi-select: list of ids) — Advance by
      swipe: Swipe (e.g. Mobile)
      arrow-buttons: Arrow buttons (e.g. Netflix on web)
      dots: Dots (e.g. Hero banners)
      autoplay: Autoplay (e.g. Marketing heroes)
* Timing [lifecycle] — Does it move on its own?
  - autoplay (single-select: one id) — Autoplay
      off: Off (e.g. Netflix)
      timed-pausing-on-interaction: Timed, pausing on interaction (e.g. Retail heroes)

## text-field — Text field (component, archetype enter-data)
A single- or multi-line input for typed text, together with its label, help and validation.
Aliases: input, text box, text area
Anatomy: Label (What is asked); Input (Where text goes); Supporting text (Hint, counter or error)
Related — neighbors: autocomplete, inline-edit
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Supporting content [content] — What surrounds the input?
  - supporting (multi-select: list of ids) — Supporting content
      label: Label (e.g. All)
      placeholder: Placeholder (e.g. Search boxes)
      hint-text: Hint text (e.g. GOV.UK)
      character-counter: Character counter (e.g. Material text fields)
      prefix-or-suffix: Prefix or suffix (e.g. Currency and units)
      clear-button: Clear button (e.g. Search fields)
      format-examples: Format examples — A worked example of the expected format (e.g. QQ 12 34 56 C) shown alongside the field — the 'form' entry's Help dimension has this exact variation, but this entry's Supporting-content options don't. (e.g. GOV.UK — National Insurance number field)
      reveal-toggle: Reveal toggle — An eye/show icon toggles a sensitive value between masked dots and its plain text, distinct from a label, placeholder, hint, counter, prefix/suffix or clear button. (e.g. TurboTax — Social Security number)
* Validation [feedback] — How is input checked?
  - validation (single-select: one id) — Validation
      none: None (e.g. Free text)
      on-leaving-the-field: On leaving the field (e.g. Email fields)
      while-typing: While typing (e.g. Character limits)
      strength-meter: Strength meter (e.g. Password strength meter (Tidwell))
      on-submit: On submit — The field is checked only when the form or step is submitted (GOV.UK, Google sign-in Next, Amazon Apply) (e.g. GOV.UK — National Insurance number field)
* Style [layout] — How is the field drawn?
  - style (single-select: one id) — Style
      outlined: Outlined (e.g. Material outlined)
      filled: Filled (e.g. Material filled)
      underline-only: Underline only (e.g. Material 1)
      borderless-inline: Borderless inline (e.g. Notion)
* Assistance [initiative] — What does the system add while typing?
  - assistance (multi-select: list of ids) — Assistance
      none: None (e.g. Code fields)
      autofill: Autofill (e.g. Browser autofill)
      suggestions: Suggestions (e.g. Autocomplete)
      autocorrect-and-prediction: Autocorrect and prediction (e.g. iOS keyboard)
      rewrite: Rewrite (e.g. Writing tools in iOS)
* Input type [adaptation] — How does the field adapt to what is typed?
  - inputType (single-select: one id) — Input type
      plain: Plain (e.g. Name fields)
      specialized-keyboard: Specialized keyboard (e.g. Numeric keypad on mobile)
      masked-format: Masked format (e.g. Card numbers)
      forgiving-format: Forgiving format — Any format accepted and normalized (e.g. Forgiving format (Tidwell))
      obscured-entry: Obscured entry — The characters are hidden as they are typed, usually with a reveal toggle — a password or secret field (e.g. Apple Account — Password with rules)

## choice-control — Choice control (component, archetype enter-data)
A control for picking one or several options from a known set.
Aliases: radio buttons, checkboxes, select, segmented control, switch
Anatomy: Options (The set); Selection (What is chosen); Label (What is being chosen)
Related — neighbors: tag-input, filter-controls

* Cardinality [scope] — How many can be chosen?

      multiple-choice: Multiple choice (e.g. Checkboxes)

      ranked-order: Ranked order (e.g. Ranked-choice ballots)
